title: Strong Nouns — Masculine a-Stems
subtitle: Stān, dæg, hlāf — the largest class.
objectives: Understand and apply the concepts of Strong Nouns — Masculine a-Stems.
Read and parse examples from authentic Old English texts.

sections.heading: Core concept
sections.body: The strong masculine a-stem declension is the most common noun pattern in Old English. These nouns end in a consonant in the nominative singular. Most masculine nouns belong to this class.

sections.heading: Example
sections.body: Stān (stone): se stān (the stone, nom), þone stān (acc), þæs stānes (gen), þǣm stāne (dat). Plural: þā stānas (nom/acc), þāra stāna (gen), þǣm stānum (dat).

items.prompt: What is the main concept of this lesson?

items.answer: Review the paradigm and example above.
